The 2024 text includes 'Professional Visualization' while 2025 adds 'Automotive', but the core subject of transition complexity remains identical.

The current disclosure D008 elaborates on this specific topic of launch cadence, citing the computing industry's broader and faster launch of accelerated computing platforms and NVIDIA's new cadence of completing new computing solutions each year. This is a specific subset of the transition complexity topic.

The previous disclosure D007 discusses how transitions impact the ability to predict demand and incur additional costs (S008). comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose that channel partner inventory adjustments preceding new product introductions or due to market normalization contribute to revenue volatility and declines. NVDA specifically cites 'channel partners reducing channel inventory of prior architectures' as a cause for revenue reductions or volatility during complex product transitions. Similarly, AMD attributes its significant 33% Embedded revenue decrease to customers normalizing inventory levels, demonstrating a shared operational risk where supply chain inventory dynamics, driven by product cycles or demand shifts, impact reported revenue performance.

sentences.text: Qualification time for new products, customers anticipating product transitions and channel partners reducing channel inventory of prior architectures ahead of new product introductions can create reductions or volatility in our revenue.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.
